title: Chapter 122 — Toward Store Leadership
intro: The second crossing — from sales manager to store leader, the P&L chair, and the strategic rhythm.

sections.title: The P&L Is Now Your Job
sections.content:
As a sales manager, you owned the top line. As a store leader, you own everything — revenue, margin, expenses, payroll, inventory, shrink, and profitability.

This is the second crossing. Selling is now one part of a much larger picture. You need to understand how every dollar comes in and where every dollar goes.

The best store leaders were great salespeople who learned to think like business owners. The P&L is not a report you glance at. It is the scorecard of your business.

sections.title: Strategic Rhythm
sections.content:
Store leadership requires a rhythm: daily floor checks, weekly team reviews, monthly financial analysis, quarterly strategic planning.

Without rhythm, you are reactive — putting out fires instead of building something. With rhythm, you catch problems early, develop people consistently, and make decisions based on data instead of instinct.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating store leadership readiness, ask:

Does the leader understand the full P&L — not just the sales line?
Do they have a strategic rhythm — or are they purely reactive?
Do they balance floor time with operational responsibility?
Are they building a business — or just managing a store?
